[b][color=#00ff00]Why built this mod when we have another similar one?

[/color][/b][list]
[*]This offers GMCM menu allows customization
[*]Shortcut F8: Overlay Highlights soil that is currently benefiting from Natural Irrigation.
[*]Added optional function: Tiles within the High Moisture Radius (default: 1 tile from water) are considered in a high-moisture zone, therefore there is some chance for it to grow faster

Crops planted right next to water [i]should[/i] benefit from it – not behave the same as a lonely patch in the middle of a field.

[b]Natural Irrigation[/b] makes water proximity actually matter: soil near rivers, ponds, and other water tiles starts the day hydrated,

and crops growing in the “extra moist” zone have a chance to grow a little faster.

Everything is configurable and designed to feel like a natural extension of vanilla gameplay, not a cheat.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/39932/39932-1764969135-978029311.png[/img]

[line][b][color=#00ffff]What the mod does
[/color][/b]
🌊 Water-fed soil based on distance to water

Each morning, the mod looks at your tilled soil and checks how close it is to natural water sources:
[list]
[*]Rivers
[*]Ponds
[*]Any tile on the map marked as “Water”
[/list]If a tile is within the [b]water search radius[/b] (configurable), that soil starts the day [b]watered[/b], as if it stayed moist overnight thanks to nearby water.

[list]
[*]Default radius: [b]4 tiles[/b]
[*]Can be lowered, raised, or disabled entirely (radius 0)
[/list]Mechanically this is still Stardew’s watering system, but the [i]reason[/i] your soil is wet is now tied to the landscape instead of just tools and sprinklers.
[line][b][color=#00ffff]💧 Moisture tiers & growth bonuses
[/color][/b]
Not all irrigated soil is equal. Tiles very close to water are treated as extra moist:

[list]
[*]Tiles within the [b]High Moisture Radius[/b] (default: 1 tile from water) are considered in a [b]high-moisture zone[/b].
[*]Crops growing on those tiles have a [b]configurable chance per day[/b] to gain an [b]extra day of growth progress[/b]:
[list]
[*]They advance faster through their current growth phase.
[*]Fully grown crops are not affected.
[*]No items or stats are changed, just growth speed.
[/list][/list]Config options:

[list]
[*][b]High moisture radius[/b] – how close crops must be to water to qualify (in tiles).
[*][b]Growth chance (%)[/b] – the daily chance that eligible crops get the extra growth tick.
[/list]This makes shorelines, riverbanks, and pond edges feel like genuinely valuable farming spots without being over-the-top.
[line][b][color=#00ffff]🧪 Optional Natural Irrigation overlay (debug tool)
[/color][/b]
For players who like to understand exactly what a mod is doing, there’s an optional debug overlay:

[list]
[*]Highlights soil that is currently benefiting from Natural Irrigation.
[*]Shows [b]irrigated tiles[/b] and [b]high-moisture tiles[/b] in different tints.
[*]The overlay is [b]OFF by default[/b] – it won’t appear in normal play unless you enable it and toggle it on.
[*]You can:
[list]
[*]Allow/disallow the overlay in the config.
[*]Set a custom [b]toggle key[/b] (default: [code]F8[/code]) to turn it on/off in-game.
[/list][/list]Use it to plan farm layouts or just to satisfy your curiosity about how far the water’s influence reaches.
[line][b][color=#00ffff]Configuration[/color][/b]

All settings are configurable.

In-game (with GMCM)If you install [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b], you can manage everything from the title screen or pause menu:

[list]
[*][b]Enable Natural Irrigation[/b]
Turn the entire effect on or off.[*][b]Water search radius[/b]
How many tiles from water still count as “naturally irrigated”.[*][b]High moisture radius[/b]
The radius where soil is considered extra moist and can get growth bonuses.[*][b]Growth chance (%)[/b]
Chance per day for crops in the high-moisture zone to gain extra growth progress.[*][b]Allow overlay[/b]
Whether the debug overlay feature is available at all (it still starts hidden).[*][b]Overlay toggle key[/b]
Which key toggles the overlay in-game (default [code]F8[/code]).[/list]Manual config.jsonIf you don’t use GMCM, the mod will generate a [code]config.json[/code] after you run the game once.
You can edit it with any text editor while the game is closed.
[list]
[/list][line][b][color=#00ffff]Compatibility
[/color][/b]
[list]
[*]Designed for [b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b] and [b]SMAPI 4.x[/b].
[*]Works with:
[list]
[*]All standard farm types
[*]Most custom maps, as long as they use normal water tiles or mark water properly
[/list][*]Doesn’t edit vanilla assets or XNBs.
[*]Doesn’t add new items or buff systems – it only influences soil state and crop growth logic.
[*]Should be safe to add or remove mid-save. Tiles will simply stop or start benefiting from Natural Irrigation depending on whether the mod is installed/active.
[/list]
